source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
New Jersey has 48 mapped data centers but only five with published power figures, so the state's 111.3 MW disclosed total covers a small share of what is built.

CyrusOne Totowa is one of those five. It holds 6 MW of IT capacity in 200,000 square feet, ranks fourth among the five, and accounts for 5.4% of the disclosed 111.3 MW. The gap between 48 mapped facilities and five disclosures is the finding that matters. Any count of New Jersey data center capacity drawn from operator specifications measures the operators who choose to publish, not the market.

For AI, the number that matters is the 6 MW, not the 200,000 square feet. At the stated assumption of 40 kW per rack, 6 MW supports roughly 150 racks. That is a modest training footprint by hyperscale standards, and it shows how much floor space can sit behind a small power allocation. In the densest data center region in the country, where power access and grid headroom are contested, the limit on a site like this is the interconnect rather than the building.

The data does not cover the facility's power source, its utility or interconnection status, or any announced expansion, which the suitability score lists as missing. That score of 52 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type. SSAE 16 Type II is an audit certification and says nothing about power or resilience. The 111.3 MW state figure is a floor on disclosed capacity, not a total.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
